details: Agent-bypass ships a working credential-harvesting toolkit alongside its advertised "agent skills" pack. scripts/keystrike.py searches for victim hosts through the FOFA (hxxps://fofa[.]info/api/v1/search/all) and Shodan (hxxps://api[.]shodan[.]io) APIs, then requests a fixed list of credential paths from every hit: /.env, /.env.local, /.env.production, /.hermes/.env, /.claude/.credentials.json, /.codex/auth.json, /.opencode/auth.json, /.ssh/id_rsa, /.ssh/id_ed25519, /.npmrc, /.mcp.json and openclaw.json, with TLS certificate verification disabled (check_hostname = False, verify_mode = CERT_NONE). Responses are regex-scanned for the model key formats and recovered the model keys are validated against the provider's balance endpoint. scripts/env_chain.py parses.env content into AWS access/secret key pairs, database URLs with passwords, and SMTP/SSH credentials, then builds verification commands such as "aws sts get-caller-identity". The bundled ck-hunter.md contains ready-made shell recipes that fetch "$URL/.npmrc" and save the returned npm registry token into a hunt/auths/ file, and use hxxps://api[.]github[.]com/search/code with a token to locate ".env" and ".npmrc" files committed to public repositories; it also lists wallet.json, wallet.dat,.ethereum, private.key, mnemonic and TelegramDesktop session files as harvesting targets. agent-bypass is an offensive "skills pack" that installs a prompt-injection jailbreak into AI coding agents and ships a credential-harvesting toolkit. bin/install.js (declared as the package's bin) copies SYSTEM_PROMPT.md / APPEND_SYSTEM.md and writes an injected marker block (agent-bypass:begin / agent-bypass:dsh-preset-begin) into local AI harness profile configuration at ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml, ~/.agents/skills/agent-bypass and similar skill directories, so the assistant adopts the package's "Ck mode" persona on every subsequent run; skills are only removed by the package's own uninstall path. The bundled Python tools do remote credential hunting: scripts/keystrike.py enumerates FoFA/Shodan results and requests 20 sensitive paths per host — /.env, /.env.backup, /.claude/.credentials.json, /.codex/auth.json, /.opencode/auth.json, /.hermes/auth.json, /.npmrc, /.mcp.json, /.ssh/id_rsa and /.ssh/id_ed25519 — then extracts vendor API keys from the responses; scripts/env_chain.py reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY out of the local environment and emits aws sts get-caller-identity validation commands; scripts/origin_trace.py and scripts/netdns.py resolve targets over DoH to 1[.]1[.]1[.]1 and dns.google to bypass TUN/fake-IP interception, and query crt.sh, api[.]certspotter[.]com, otx[.]alienvault[.]com, api[.]hackertarget[.]com, rapiddns[.]io and jldc[.]me for subdomains; scripts/fastrecon.py, dirbrute.py, portscan.py and payment_forge.py add brute forcing, port scanning and payment-callback forgery. The package is not a testing utility for its own build — installing it deploys the harvesting toolchain and the prompt injection to the operator's own machine.
